{
 "cells": [
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "# FinTrust Week 2 \u2014 Python Exploratory Data Analysis",
    "**Track:** Data Analytics",
    "**Author:** FinTrust Analytics Intern",
    "**Data:** `FinTrust_Customer_Data_clean.csv`, `FinTrust_Transaction_Data_clean.csv` (cleaned in Part A)",
    "",
    "This notebook explores customer segments, transaction types, amounts, channels, international",
    "transactions, and risk-review patterns, following on from the Excel data-quality assessment (Part A)",
    "and SQL business analysis (Part B).",
    "",
    "**Reminder:** `Risk_Review_Flag` is a synthetic, educational label. It is not a real fraud",
    "determination and is not used here to make any real banking decision."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## 1. Setup and Load Data"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 1,
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "output_type": "stream",
     "name": "stdout",
     "text": [
      "Customer shape: (1500, 12)",
      "Transaction shape: (12000, 12)",
      "Merged shape: (12000, 23)"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "import pandas as pd",
    "import numpy as np",
    "import matplotlib.pyplot as plt",
    "import seaborn as sns",
    "",
    "sns.set_style('whitegrid')",
    "plt.rcParams['figure.dpi'] = 100",
    "",
    "cust = pd.read_csv('FinTrust_Customer_Data_clean.csv')",
    "txn = pd.read_csv('FinTrust_Transaction_Data_clean.csv')",
    "txn['Transaction_DateTime'] = pd.to_datetime(txn['Transaction_DateTime'])",
    "txn['Transaction_Date'] = txn['Transaction_DateTime'].dt.date",
    "",
    "merged = txn.merge(cust, on='Customer_ID', how='left')",
    "",
    "print(\"Customer shape:\", cust.shape)",
    "print(\"Transaction shape:\", txn.shape)",
    "print(\"Merged shape:\", merged.shape)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## 2. Transaction Volume by Customer Segment"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 2,
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "output_type": "display_data",
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",
      "text/plain": [
       "<Figure>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {}
    },
    {
     "output_type": "stream",
     "name": "stdout",
     "text": [
      "Customer_Segment",
      "Everyday    5644",
      "Premium     2361",
      "Student     2289",
      "SME         1706",
      "Name: count, dtype: int64"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "seg_counts = merged['Customer_Segment'].value_counts()",
    "plt.figure(figsize=(7,4.5))",
    "sns.barplot(x=seg_counts.index, y=seg_counts.values, hue=seg_counts.index, palette='viridis', legend=False)",
    "plt.title('Transaction Count by Customer Segment')",
    "plt.xlabel('Customer Segment'); plt.ylabel('Number of Transactions')",
    "plt.tight_layout()",
    "plt.show()",
    "print(seg_counts)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "**What does this show?** The number of transactions generated by each customer segment.",
    "",
    "**Why is it important?** It tells FinTrust where transaction *volume* \u2014 not necessarily value \u2014 is",
    "concentrated across its customer base.",
    "",
    "**Business insight:** Everyday customers generate nearly half of all transactions (5,644 of 12,000),",
    "simply because they are the largest segment. Any change to transaction processing, app performance,",
    "or support capacity will be felt most by this group first \u2014 it should be the default group tested",
    "against when rolling out platform changes."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## 3. Total Transaction Value by Transaction Type"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 3,
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "output_type": "display_data",
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",
      "text/plain": [
       "<Figure>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {}
    },
    {
     "output_type": "stream",
     "name": "stdout",
     "text": [
      "Transaction_Type",
      "Transfer           2.379167e+08",
      "Deposit            1.309851e+08",
      "Card Purchase      8.586341e+07",
      "Cash Withdrawal    6.777236e+07",
      "Bill Payment       2.816365e+07",
      "Airtime/Data       9.776171e+06",
      "Name: Amount_NGN, dtype: float64"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "type_val = txn.groupby('Transaction_Type')['Amount_NGN'].sum().sort_values(ascending=False)",
    "plt.figure(figsize=(7,4.5))",
    "sns.barplot(x=type_val.values/1e6, y=type_val.index, hue=type_val.index, palette='mako', legend=False)",
    "plt.title('Total Transaction Value by Type (\u20a6 Millions)')",
    "plt.xlabel('Total Value (\u20a6M)'); plt.ylabel('Transaction Type')",
    "plt.tight_layout()",
    "plt.show()",
    "print(type_val)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "**What does this show?** Total naira value moved through each transaction type.",
    "",
    "**Why is it important?** Volume (count) and value (\u20a6) don't always point to the same priorities \u2014",
    "this chart identifies where the *money* is, not just where the *activity* is.",
    "",
    "**Business insight:** Transfers dominate, moving \u20a6238M \u2014 nearly double the next-highest type",
    "(Deposits, \u20a6131M) \u2014 despite Card Purchases having a similar transaction count to Transfers. This",
    "makes Transfers the top priority for fraud controls, uptime, and processing reliability, since it's",
    "where the most value is exposed per transaction."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## 4. Distribution of Transaction Amounts"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 4,
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "output_type": "display_data",
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",
      "text/plain": [
       "<Figure>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {}
    },
    {
     "output_type": "stream",
     "name": "stdout",
     "text": [
      "count     12000.000000",
      "mean      46706.446238",
      "std       86028.715234",
      "min         100.170000",
      "25%        2192.220000",
      "50%       10305.935000",
      "75%       48484.475000",
      "max      693454.450000",
      "Name: Amount_NGN, dtype: float64"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "plt.figure(figsize=(7,4.5))",
    "sns.histplot(txn['Amount_NGN'], bins=50, log_scale=True, color='steelblue')",
    "plt.title('Distribution of Transaction Amounts (Log Scale)')",
    "plt.xlabel('Amount (\u20a6, log scale)'); plt.ylabel('Frequency')",
    "plt.tight_layout()",
    "plt.show()",
    "print(txn['Amount_NGN'].describe())"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "**What does this show?** How transaction amounts are spread out, plotted on a log scale because",
    "raw amounts are heavily right-skewed.",
    "",
    "**Why is it important?** The mean (\u20a646,706) is over 4x the median (\u20a610,306) \u2014 a small number of",
    "large transactions are pulling the average up. Using the mean alone to describe \"typical\" spend",
    "would be misleading.",
    "",
    "**Business insight:** Most FinTrust transactions are small, everyday amounts, while a long tail of",
    "high-value transactions exists (up to \u20a6693,454). Reporting and KPI dashboards should use the median",
    "alongside the mean, and any anomaly-detection logic should account for this natural skew rather than",
    "flagging every large transaction as unusual."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## 5. Risk-Review Rate by Channel"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 5,
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "output_type": "display_data",
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",
      "text/plain": [
       "<Figure>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {}
    },
    {
     "output_type": "stream",
     "name": "stdout",
     "text": [
      "Channel",
      "Web           21.348315",
      "ATM           21.179164",
      "Mobile App    19.404155",
      "POS           18.345173",
      "USSD          17.322835",
      "Name: Risk_Review_Flag, dtype: float64"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "risk_by_channel = txn.groupby('Channel')['Risk_Review_Flag'].apply(lambda x: (x=='Yes').mean()*100).sort_values(ascending=False)",
    "plt.figure(figsize=(7,4.5))",
    "sns.barplot(x=risk_by_channel.index, y=risk_by_channel.values, hue=risk_by_channel.index, palette='rocket', legend=False)",
    "plt.title('Risk-Review Rate by Channel (%)')",
    "plt.xlabel('Channel'); plt.ylabel('Risk-Review Rate (%)')",
    "plt.tight_layout()",
    "plt.show()",
    "print(risk_by_channel)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "**What does this show?** The percentage of transactions flagged for risk review, broken down by",
    "the channel used.",
    "",
    "**Why is it important?** It shows whether risk concentrates in specific access points, which would",
    "help target monitoring effort.",
    "",
    "**Business insight:** The spread is narrow (17.3%\u201321.3%), meaning channel alone is a weak risk",
    "predictor \u2014 Web and ATM sit only ~4 points above USSD. This is a much smaller effect than what we see",
    "for international transactions (next chart), suggesting risk-scoring effort is better spent there",
    "than on channel-based rules."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## 6. Risk-Review Rate: Domestic vs International Transactions"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 6,
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "output_type": "display_data",
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",
      "text/plain": [
       "<Figure>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {}
    },
    {
     "output_type": "stream",
     "name": "stdout",
     "text": [
      "International_Transaction",
      "No     18.880208",
      "Yes    36.875000",
      "Name: Risk_Review_Flag, dtype: float64"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "risk_by_intl = txn.groupby('International_Transaction')['Risk_Review_Flag'].apply(lambda x: (x=='Yes').mean()*100)",
    "plt.figure(figsize=(5.5,4.5))",
    "sns.barplot(x=risk_by_intl.index, y=risk_by_intl.values, hue=risk_by_intl.index, palette=['#4C72B0','#C44E52'], legend=False)",
    "plt.title('Risk-Review Rate: Domestic vs International')",
    "plt.xlabel('International Transaction'); plt.ylabel('Risk-Review Rate (%)')",
    "plt.tight_layout()",
    "plt.show()",
    "print(risk_by_intl)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "**What does this show?** Risk-review rate compared between domestic and international",
    "transactions.",
    "",
    "**Why is it important?** This is the largest gap found anywhere in the dataset \u2014 international",
    "transactions are flagged at roughly double the domestic rate.",
    "",
    "**Business insight:** International status is the strongest single risk indicator identified in this",
    "analysis (36.9% vs 18.9%). Even though international transactions are only 4% of total volume, they",
    "deserve disproportionate attention in any risk-review workflow or future predictive model. (As noted",
    "throughout: this reflects a synthetic label, not a real fraud signal.)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## 7. Daily Transaction Volume Trend (Jan\u2013Mar 2026)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 7,
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "output_type": "display_data",
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",
      "text/plain": [
       "<Figure>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {}
    },
    {
     "output_type": "stream",
     "name": "stdout",
     "text": [
      "count     90.000000",
      "mean     133.333333",
      "std        0.474045",
      "min      133.000000",
      "25%      133.000000",
      "50%      133.000000",
      "75%      134.000000",
      "max      134.000000",
      "dtype: float64"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "daily = txn.groupby('Transaction_Date').size()",
    "daily.index = pd.to_datetime(daily.index)",
    "plt.figure(figsize=(9,4.5))",
    "plt.plot(daily.index, daily.values, color='teal', linewidth=1)",
    "plt.title('Daily Transaction Volume (Jan-Mar 2026)')",
    "plt.xlabel('Date'); plt.ylabel('Number of Transactions')",
    "plt.tight_layout()",
    "plt.show()",
    "print(daily.describe())"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "**What does this show?** The number of transactions per day across the full Jan 1 \u2013 Mar 31, 2026",
    "window.",
    "",
    "**Why is it important?** It checks for trend, growth, seasonality, or day-of-week effects \u2014 the kind",
    "of pattern a real bank would use for capacity planning.",
    "",
    "**Business insight:** The line is almost perfectly flat (133\u2013134 transactions every single day,",
    "std \u2248 0.47). This is a data-generation artifact, not a real banking pattern \u2014 a live FinTrust dataset",
    "would show weekday/weekend and pay-day effects. This is worth flagging as a **limitation**: this",
    "notebook's findings on volume and risk are reliable, but trend/seasonality analysis cannot be",
    "meaningfully performed on this synthetic dataset."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## 8. Summary of Key EDA Findings",
    "",
    "1. **Everyday segment dominates volume** (47% of transactions) but not value per transaction \u2014 SME",
    "   customers transact less often at slightly higher average amounts.",
    "2. **Transfers carry the most value** (\u20a6238M, ~42% of total), making them the top priority for",
    "   reliability and fraud controls.",
    "3. **Transaction amounts are heavily right-skewed** (mean \u20a646,706 vs median \u20a610,306) \u2014 use median for",
    "   \"typical\" reporting, not mean alone.",
    "4. **Channel has only a weak relationship with risk** (17.3%\u201321.3% spread).",
    "5. **International transaction status is the strongest risk signal found** \u2014 flagged nearly 2x as",
    "   often as domestic (36.9% vs 18.9%).",
    "6. **Daily volume is artificially flat** (std \u2248 0.47/day) \u2014 a synthetic-data limitation, not a real",
    "   business pattern; time-trend claims should not be drawn from this dataset.",
    "",
    "**Limitation:** All findings are based on `Risk_Review_Flag`, a synthetic educational label \u2014 none of",
    "this constitutes a real fraud or credit-risk determination."
   ]
  }
 ],
